actions.action: Confirm external user impact and affected critical journeys.
Declare a provisional severity from user impact and integrity risk.
Freeze deployments, migrations and discretionary jobs.
Assign incident commander, operations lead, communications lead and scribe.
Open the incident channel and UTC event timeline.
Classify edge, ingress, compute, database, cache, queue or dependency involvement.
Check for hostile traffic, credential abuse, privilege changes and evidence loss.
Apply the least destructive available containment from a linked runbook.
Separate legitimate demand from hostile traffic before changing admission.
Use the documented manual rollback only when a revision correlation and known-good target are established.
Stop optional load and prevent uncontrolled scale or retries from exhausting the database.
Fail fast or disable optional dependency work instead of accumulating concurrency.
Engage the affected cloud or service provider through an approved support route.
Publish the first factual impact and next-checkpoint update.
Verify containment through external journeys and each affected region.
Choose normal, degraded, read-only or unavailable mode without claiming an unavailable switch exists.
Validate write outcomes, replication state, queue age, retries and dead letters.
Confirm telemetry and page receipt; use a secondary route if either is unverified.
Set the next decision time, authority and evidence required.
Update responders and users with confirmed impact, containment and next checkpoint.

runbooks.title: Sudden load or Layer 7 abuse
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-SUDDEN-LOAD-OR-L7
runbooks.trigger: Critical SLO burn, origin saturation, cache-bypass pattern or hostile request flood.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Freeze changes, classify legitimate demand versus abuse, and stop optional work using only controls that actually exist.
prohibitedActions: Do not scale the origin without checking database and cost budgets.
Do not block all shared-IP or provider traffic without validating legitimate cohorts.
recoveryValidation: Critical synthetic journeys and both burn windows recover.
Origin, database and cost saturation return below approved limits.
evidencePreservation: Record WAF, cache, route, identity, region and revision summaries.
Record every policy or traffic mutation with UTC time and approver.

runbooks.title: Database saturation or integrity uncertainty
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-DATABASE-INTEGRITY
runbooks.trigger: Pool exhaustion, writer uncertainty, corruption signal, unsafe replica lag or failed database primary.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Stop optional load and retries, freeze changes, and determine whether acknowledged writes have a known outcome.
prohibitedActions: Do not retry unknown commits or perform destructive rollback.
Do not promote or reopen writes without an approved recovery point and dual control.
recoveryValidation: Data integrity checks and critical read/write journeys pass.
Connection, lock, lag and transaction signals remain stable through staged reopen.
evidencePreservation: Capture timestamps, transaction/error classes, pool and replication state without query values.
Preserve candidate revision, migration digest and recovery-point identifiers.

runbooks.title: Bad application deployment
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-BAD-DEPLOYMENT
runbooks.trigger: Errors, latency or user failures correlate with the current revision or configuration change.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Freeze changes, identify the immutable last-known-good revision, then use the approved manual rollback procedure.
prohibitedActions: Do not roll the database schema backward destructively.
Do not choose a revision that has not passed the required candidate checks.
recoveryValidation: External smoke and critical journeys pass on the restored revision.
Error and latency burn recover without data inconsistency.
evidencePreservation: Record image digest, revision, configuration digest and traffic percentages.
Preserve deployment logs and the UTC rollback decision.

runbooks.title: Queue backlog or poison message
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-QUEUE-BACKLOG
runbooks.trigger: Oldest critical job breaches its SLO, retries rise, dead letters appear or workers threaten a downstream budget.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Reduce producer and worker pressure using available service-specific controls; quarantine poison messages without blind replay.
prohibitedActions: Do not scale workers past database or provider limits.
Do not purge or replay messages without idempotency and scope evidence.
recoveryValidation: Arrival is below completion and oldest age trends down inside the SLO.
Critical outcomes reconcile and dead letters are scoped.
evidencePreservation: Capture queue age, depth, arrival, completion, retry and dead-letter counts.
Record message schema and safe identifiers, never sensitive payloads.

runbooks.title: Upload, scanner or storage incident
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-UPLOAD-PIPELINE
runbooks.trigger: Scanner unavailable or stale, storage errors, malicious content signal or uncontrolled upload cost.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Preserve quarantine and stop attachment/finalisation; do not claim upload signing is disabled until the missing switch exists.
prohibitedActions: Do not make quarantined objects public or bypass scanning.
Do not delete suspected malicious evidence before security review.
recoveryValidation: Scanner freshness, signed upload, quarantine and clean-download staging tests pass.
Backlog drains within storage, scanner and database budgets.
evidencePreservation: Record object-safe identifiers, scan verdicts and definition age without signed URLs.
Preserve quarantined evidence under approved retention controls.

runbooks.title: Sydney application or database outage
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-REGIONAL-OUTAGE
runbooks.trigger: Independent probes confirm a Sydney regional failure or primary database loss.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Freeze changes, verify Melbourne capacity and replication evidence, and remain degraded rather than improvising promotion.
prohibitedActions: Do not promote an unverified database secondary or create split brain.
Do not shift traffic into a region without N-1 capacity and dependency checks.
recoveryValidation: Regional synthetic journeys, data recovery point and queue state are validated.
Failback and reconciliation authority are recorded before normal writes resume.
evidencePreservation: Capture regional health, replication lag, recovery point and traffic state.
Record every ejection, promotion and DNS or load-balancer decision.

runbooks.title: Realtime provider or broadcast degradation
runbooks.heading: RB-IR-REALTIME-SIDE-EFFECT
runbooks.trigger: Realtime provider latency, error or fan-out threatens the critical application path.
runbooks.safeFirstAction: Confirm the critical path is independent, then prepare a reviewed revision that suppresses realtime broadcast.
prohibitedActions: Do not bypass authorization or expose private channel data.
Do not hot-edit production outside the protected workflow.
recoveryValidation: Critical journeys remain healthy with broadcast suppressed.
Staging proves authorized broadcast before restoration.
evidencePreservation: Record provider health, broadcast errors, revision and affected operation counts.
Preserve safe correlation IDs without message content.
